column1: # bash-guards.tsv — read by bash-guards.sh: name, PCRE regex (grep -zP over the whole command; anchored rows carry (?m)), deny reason, optional token-level exemption regex.

# `$name`/`${name}` in a regex or reason resolves once from secret-shapes.sh or the prefixes bash-guards.sh defines. The first matching row denies. Reason prefixes are read by cases, smokes and live traces: never respell them.
# The requests-* rows match the whole command, so their exemption judges the whole command: a plain read passes, anything else that names the place is refused.

column3: secret-in-argv-guard: REFUSED — a credential-shaped NAME=value carries a literal; $route.
secret-in-argv-guard: REFUSED — a credential flag carries a literal value; $route.
secret-in-argv-guard: REFUSED — a literal Bearer token is on the command line; $route.
secret-in-argv-guard: REFUSED — an sk-<vendor>- key shape is on the command line; $route.
owned-process-guard: REFUSED — pkill -f matches every process whose command line carries the pattern; $by_identity
owned-process-guard: REFUSED — killall matches every process by name; $by_identity
owned-process-guard: REFUSED — a process list matched by name feeds kill; $by_identity
owned-process-guard: REFUSED — kill -1 signals every process you own; $by_identity

column1: # The owner and merge rows match literal spellings that an agent writes,
# quoted program names and the path forms /./ and //.
# The owner unit row assigns word roles once, from left to right.
# systemctl --help and loginctl --help of systemd 261 supply the lists.
# Atomic choices try redirections, option-value pairs, other options, then positional words.
# Only other options can give help. Only positional words can be verbs.
# The first known systemctl verb decides. Unknown positional words do not decide.
# A later unit name cannot change that choice. No known verb means a unit list.
# The loginctl check still refuses each status verb in a positional role.
# A value option skips redirections before its value.
# Shared captures retain role flags across alternatives in both PCRE and Perl.
# A chosen forbidden verb needs no segment end. The no-known-verb check needs an end.
# A closing shell-string quote ends the pass. The outer suffix does not matter.
# The pass reads all known roles so a later help option still exempts the command.
# Redirections include here strings, clobber forms, read-write forms and fd copies.
# A short bundle takes the next word only if its first value letter ends it.
# Quote splitting inside a word, globs, brace expansion, variables, eval
# and command substitution are out of scope.

column3: owner-secret-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule does not permit process arguments in output. Use ps -eo pid,etime,comm.
owner-secret-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule does not permit process arguments in output. Use ps -eo pid,etime,comm.

owner-secret-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule does not permit process arguments or environment values in output. A unit list, a unit status or a cgroup tree prints the command line of each process. Use systemctl is-active <unit> or systemctl show -p ActiveState,SubState,MainPID <unit>.
owner-secret-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule does not permit reads of process arguments or environment files. Do not read these files. Use ps -eo pid,etime,comm.
owner-secret-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule does not permit reads of the secret environment file. Do not read or source this file. Use the service that owns the required value.
merge-evidence-guard: REFUSED — use gh pr merge <number> --match-head-commit <full sha> with reviewed head evidence.
review-cap: REFUSED — only a counted reader door may call review admit. Use nspawn_review_start or a new unnamed Agent reviewer.
merge-evidence-guard: REFUSED — the owner rule requires merge evidence. Add a Regression delta: line and a Review: line with SHIP to the PR body.
release-guard: REFUSED — git push targets a public member repository. Only the release workflow, triggered by the owner's merge into public, writes there. Open a release PR into public instead.

release-guard: REFUSED — git push targets the public branch. Only the owner's merge of a release PR writes public, and the release workflow then publishes. Push a release/vX.Y.Z branch and open its PR instead.
trunk-guard: REFUSED — git push targets the trunk; main/master lands by pull request, or by $grant. Push the lane branch and name the merge as the next act.
trunk-guard: REFUSED — a force push rewrites history others hold; it needs $grant. Push to a new branch name instead.
trunk-guard: REFUSED — git push --delete removes a remote branch; it needs $grant. Leave the branch and name it in your report.
trunk-guard: REFUSED — git branch -D/-d/--delete removes a branch; it needs $grant. Leave the branch and name it in your report.

trunk-guard: REFUSED — git stash moves work off the tree (the stack is shared across worktrees); it needs $grant. Commit the work to a new branch in your own worktree instead. `git stash list`/`show`/`pop`/`apply` pass.

trunk-guard: REFUSED — git reset --hard discards uncommitted work; it needs $grant. In your own worktree, `git reset --keep <sha>` moves the branch and keeps uncommitted changes. Never move the primary checkout. Make a new worktree instead.

requests-guard: REFUSED — the prompt spool (a *.prompts.jsonl file under the runtime directory) is the owner's record: only plugin/hooks/prompt-capture.py appends to it, and a line that an agent writes there looks like an owner prompt or acceptance. Read it with the Read tool, or with cat, head, tail, jq or grep alone in the command (no pipe, redirect or second command).

requests-guard: REFUSED — the requests directory (nott/requests under the runtime directory) belongs to the node host: only the host and plugin/hooks/prompt-capture.py write there. Read it with the Read tool, or with cat, head, tail, ls, jq or grep alone in the command (no pipe, redirect or second command). A scratch runtime directory named by its own path is not refused.

launch-guard: REFUSED — a claude, codex or agy model session, or an ACP adapter, starts only through nSPAWN (the one-launcher rule). Never start it from the Bash tool. Start it with nspawn_run_start. These forms pass: `claude plugin|mcp|config|doctor|update`, `codex plugin|mcp|login status`, the version and help flags of claude and codex, and `claude-agent-acp --version`. For a PR title with a vendor word, put the title in a file. Then run `gh pr create --title "$(cat title.txt)" --body-file body.md`. The file content stays data.

column1: # The temp-* rows read the command without quoted grep patterns and data heredocs, like the trunk rows.
# Quote splitting inside a word, variables, `cd`, eval and command substitution are out of scope.
# An rm operand or a find start path that names only the root is refused with no glob and no name test.

column3: temp-glob-guard: REFUSED — rm names a shared temporary directory itself, or a glob or a brace list under it (${temp_places}). ${temp_cure}
temp-glob-guard: REFUSED — find deletes a shared temporary directory itself, or deletes by a name pattern under it (${temp_places}). ${temp_cure}
